question.prompt: For any real number \(a\) and positive integer \(k,\) define \[ \binom ak= \frac{\begin{gathered} a(a-1)(a-2)\cdots\\ {}\cdot(a-(k-1)) \end{gathered}} {\begin{gathered} k(k-1)(k-2)\cdots\\ {}\cdot(2)(1) \end{gathered}}. \] What is \[\binom{-\frac12}{100}\div\binom{\frac12}{100}\ ?\]

solutions.explanation:
The two long products overlap almost completely, so comparing their factors is easier than evaluating either coefficient. Their defining denominators are identical and cancel, leaving
\[
\frac{\binom{-\frac12}{100}}{\binom{\frac12}{100}}
=
\frac{\left(-\frac12\right)\left(-\frac32\right)\cdots\left(-\frac{199}{2}\right)}
{\left(\frac12\right)\left(-\frac12\right)\cdots\left(-\frac{197}{2}\right)}.
\]
Every factor is a nonzero half-integer, so the divisor is nonzero and the cancellations are valid. The common factors \(-\frac12,-\frac32,\ldots,-\frac{197}{2}\) cancel. Only the two unmatched endpoint factors remain:
\[
\frac{-199/2}{1/2}=-199.
\]
The answer is \(-199\), choice A.
solutions.title: Cancel the overlapping factors
